look_here_first: Find ONE mature compound leaf and count its leaflets. Twoleaf senna has exactly ONE PAIR of usually long, narrow lance-shaped leaflets (roughly 2–9 times longer than wide), with a small gland near their junction. This quickly separates S. lindheimeriana with 4–8 pairs, but NOT every western Senna: S. pilosior and S. bauhinioides also have one pair. Confirm leaflet proportions, flowers and pods.

morphology_keys.comparison_training: S. lindheimeriana is taller and velvety with 4–8 pairs of leaflets. S. pilosior is an annual western/desert comparison. The exactly-two-leaflet leaf is the fastest field character.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Against S. lindheimeriana: one narrow leaflet pair versus 4–8 velvety pairs. Against S. pilosior: narrower lance-shaped leaflets versus broader hairy leaflets and stiff mixed stem hairs (both perennials). Against S. bauhinioides: narrower leaflets plus reproductive style, fruit and seed characters; one pair alone is insufficient.
